text:
Alex Kim: Quick flag  the API reference still shows the embeddings example with "input": "single string" in a few places. Users are getting tripped up when they expect batching.
Sofia Herrera: Where did you spot it?
Alex Kim: openapi/embeddings.yml (example.request.body), quickstart/curl.md, and snippets/python/embeds_quickstart.py. Found via a community issue.
Ben Wallace: Our server accepts both, but canonical shape is an array: "inputs". We should make examples consistent and add a short migration note.
Sofia Herrera: Agreed. Minimal changes: replace example bodies with an array payload, update python snippet, and add a 1-2 line callout under Embeddings -> Request shape: "Use \"inputs\" array for batching; single-string \"input\" accepted for backward compatibility."
ci-bot: Lint: PR #999 example.request.body does not match OpenAPI schema (expected array but example is object) at docs/openapi/embeddings.yml:45.
docs-bot: Deploy preview failed: openapi examples must match schema.
Ben Wallace: I'll update the openapi example to:
```json
{
  "model": "rwd-embed-1",
  "inputs": ["first text", "second text"]
}
```
and change python snippet to:
```py
from redwood import Client
client = Client()
resp = client.embeddings.create(model="rwd-embed-1", inputs=["a","b"])
print(resp.data)
```
Sofia Herrera: Please also add a tiny migration note in the changelog and link it from the API page. One sentence is fine.
Alex Kim: Heads-up: also sweep the JS and Go quickstart snippets; I grepped and found two instances each where they still pass a plain string. If Ben wants, I can follow-up with a tiny PR to catch those.
Ben Wallace: I'll handle openapi + python + curl in this PR. Alex, please follow up on JS/Go in a separate PR; easier to review.
ci-bot: PR #999 updated, re-running lints.
ci-bot: All checks passed for PR #999.
docs-bot: Preview deployed.
Sofia Herrera: Merged. Thanks. I'll submit the changelog entry linking to the migration note (one-liner).
Alex Kim: Great work. Let's monitor support tickets tomorrow in case any users are still confused and add an FAQ if needed. :thumbsup:
